original_caption: 1) Neuromorphic hardware (Loihi): In this work, Intel’s neuromorphic research chip Loihi [20] in the form of a Kapoho Bay device was integrated on a rotating dual- copter. Kapoho Bay features two Loihi chips with a total of 256 neuro-cores in which a total of 262,144 neurons and up to 260 million synapses can be implemented. Three embedded x86 processors are used for monitoring and I/O spike management. | 2) Constrained UAV: The same robotic platform was used as in [8] - a constrained to 1 DoF dual-copter that can rotate 360 degrees in front of an actuated visual pattern. A 3D- printed holder was designed to mount the Kapoho Bay on top of the rotating dual-copter. Fig. 1 shows both the mounted Kapoho Bay as well as a side view of the setup.
